properties.name: A sentence the extraction could not place has no home, so the best material for the next question is rendered once and lost
properties.source: flo2 reflow2_feedback.md, 2026-09-19 addendum (F24, F25 and the meta-point)
properties.statement:
FLO2 F25. Their extraction returns `unmatched`: the clauses it could not turn into design entries, verbatim. Their point is that these are the single best material for the next question to put to the person — they are, literally, the things said that the design does not yet understand. Today they are rendered once in a transcript and then gone.

MEASURED 2026-09-20: the vocabulary DOES exist — `Fragment` with `fragment_type: note` — and nothing points at it for this. Of the served write tools, only `ingest_step`, `ingest_corpus_step` and `link_artifact` touch a Fragment at all, and each mints one as a side effect of something else (a corpus step, a registered file's provenance). `grep` finds no mention of Fragment, 'unmatched' or an unplaced utterance anywhere in the capture-intent skill.

⭐ THE REPORTER NAMES THE SHAPE THEMSELVES and they are right: it is the `EVOLVES_INTO` story again — the vocabulary existed, no instruction pointed at it, and a consumer found the hole by needing it. reflow2 recorded that lesson on 2026-08-31 after bhome hit it. THEIR ASK IN PREFERENCE ORDER: (a) a sentence in capture-intent saying unplaced utterances belong as Fragments, or (b) a named tool so it is findable by find_tools. They prefer the cheap one.
